author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Defense startup Covenant has unveiled Anthem, a ground-launched cruise missile the company says can be produced faster and at a lower price than many established long-range weapons.

The company told Reuters that Anthem carries a payload exceeding 200 kilograms and has completed more than 200 test flights over the past year. Covenant is targeting a mid-six-figure unit price once production reaches scale and says it has booked about $150 million in orders.

Founded in 2024, Covenant has raised more than $250 million and employs over 200 people in the United States, Germany and Israel. Its new Dallas plant is designed for annual capacity of 5,000 missiles; a similarly sized German facility has the same target, while an Israeli site is planned for 2,000.

Those figures are company plans, not completed production. New defense manufacturers often face certification, contracting and supply-chain obstacles when moving from tests to high-volume delivery. Covenant expects an international customer to begin receiving German-built units late this year and U.S. Army deliveries in 2027.
dek: The startup says its Anthem missile has completed more than 200 test flights and is backed by about $150 million in orders.
headline: Covenant unveils lower-cost cruise missile designed for mass production
